raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I have 600 mu — that's a big operation for around here. I am not a small household farmer; I run this like a business, but I still count every yuan because fertilizer and diesel prices keep going up.

My main land is wheat-maize rotation, like most folks in Quzhou. That's what the soil here does best and the machinery I rent is set up for it. I'll put about 450 mu into wheat-maize. The rest I split — maybe 80 mu cotton because the price has been okay and I have buyers, and 70 mu stevia because the company contracts pay decent if you hit quality.

For wheat, I plant in October. I use improved seed — Jimai or Shimai variety, whichever the dealer has good stock of. Last year I put about 20 kg urea-equivalent N per mu, plus a compound base fertilizer. I'll do the same — about 18 kg N, 8 kg P, 6 kg K. Irrigate 3 times: winter water, returning-green, and jointing. Spray maybe twice for aphids and rust. Expect around 500 kg/mu — that's what my fields gave last year.

For summer maize after wheat harvest, I use Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid. Direct seed into wheat stubble — no-till saves time because I have to turn the field around fast. About 22 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Irrigate twice if rains are short. Spray once for borer. Expect 550 kg/mu.

Cotton needs more babying — more pesticide, more water. I'll put 16 kg N, 8 kg P, 10 kg K, irrigate 5 times from wells, spray maybe 6 times for bollworm and aphids. Plough deep first. Expect 280 kg/mu seed cotton.

Stevia I learned from neighbors who contract with the factory. Needs steady water and clean fields. About 15 kg N, 10 kg P, 12 kg K. Irrigate 4 times, spray 3 times. Expect 300 kg/mu dried leaf.

I'd rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than lose yield — bad harvest on 600 mu is a disaster I cannot afford.
